correctness.rationale: Graph metric is exactly the minimum of zero- and one-rung routes. Its integer distance levels are two explicit arcs; character sums reduce to Dirichlet cosine and sine kernels and yield each spectral branch. All branches have nonzero eigenvalues; their signs give inertia. Products of odd sines and of Chebyshev roots give the two exact determinant formulas, the latter identifying the positive Pell–Lucas factor. The prism contrast follows from an explicit cut metric representation of cycle distances. A self-contained independent BFS/DFT/exact-integer determinant/Pell-product checker passed 437 assertion groups, with the analytic proof covering all n≥3. There is no reliance on finite tests as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The assembled claim is not the generic observation that a circulant matrix diagonalizes by Fourier transform. The distinct outcome is the explicit all-frequency shortest-path distance spectrum, nonsingularity and exact inertias, plus the parity-dependent determinant law (a signed power of two for odd rung count and a Pell–Lucas square for even rung count). Three directly relevant primary papers were inspected through full HTML mathematical text and theorem sections. A targeted published-mathematical-record search and a comparison with available own claims did not expose an equivalent or stronger covering statement; the residual possibility of specialized historical graph-distance literature is recorded.

value.rationale: Shortest-path distance spectra, determinants, inertia and conditional negative type are natural invariants of a canonical transitive graph family. The exact all-order classification reveals the non-obvious power-of-two versus Pell–Lucas-square parity split and linearly many positive nonconstant Fourier modes, thereby isolating an explicit mechanism whereby a Möbius twist destroys universal Gaussian positivity while the untwisted Cartesian circular ladder preserves it. The theorem supplies a meaningful infinite-family structural boundary, not just isolated numerical cases.
